summary: William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He served as Principal of the University of Edinburgh from 1762, and became a member of the Royal Society of Edinburgh and the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

William Roxburgh was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Aberdeen. He served as superintendent at Samalkot Garden and later headed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and sinologist who studied at Columbia University and the University of Michigan. He held major posts at UC Berkeley (1966–1994), City University of Hong Kong, CUHK, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

William Stede worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held an academic post at the University of London and SOAS from approximately 1928 to 1949, where he taught scholars including E. W. Adikaram, G. P. Malalasekera, and O. H. de Alwis Wijesekera.

William Van Gordon works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2015, he served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

William Ward was an Indologist and religious scholar who studied under John Fawcett at Ewood Hall Theological Academy in 1797. He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilson Hunter was an Indologist and historian who studied at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1861–1887), as vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1886), and as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society.

William Woodville Rockhill was a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr, and under Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux.

William Wright was a scholar of linguistics who studied at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. He served as Professor of Arabic at UCL (1855–1856) and Trinity College Dublin (1856–1861), and as Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (1870–1889).

Willibald Kirfel was an Indologist who completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked as a librarian in Bonn and became an ordinary professor at the University of Bonn in 1922, succeeding Jacobi.

Wilt L. Idema is a sinologist who studied at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, as well as in Japan. He served as a professor at Leiden University (1976–1999) and as Professor of Chinese Literature at Harvard University (~1999–2013).
Winfred Robert Martin worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as a librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Cornell and the University of Chicago. She served as Dean of Students at Chicago Divinity School (2000–2005) and held professorships at Washington and Lee, Buffalo, and Indiana University.
Winston Kyan works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Wu Hung, attested in 2006.

Wm. Theodore de Bary was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and Japanology who studied at Columbia University and Harvard. He served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (1953–2017) and as president of the Association for Asian Studies (1969–1970).

Wolfgang Franke was a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Berlin and the University of Hamburg. He taught at Sichuan and Peking universities before succeeding Otto Franke as the sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1977).

Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild, and at Greifswald. He taught linguistics at Greifswald and served as Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).

Wolfgang Schamoni is a scholar of Japanology who studied at Kunstakademie Düsseldorf, Waseda University, and the University of Bonn. He held positions at the universities of Marburg and Munich before serving as a professor at Heidelberg University (1985–2006).

Wolfgang Schultz was a philosopher who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna (1899–1904). He served as an administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and was Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich (1934).

Wolfram Eberhard was a scholar in sinology and history who studied in Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught in China and at Ankara University (1937–1948) before serving as Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
